# Robotics (C++/ROS2/DDS/ZMQ), Humanoid/AGV, OT/SCADA (Modbus/OPC-UA) & BESS (`robotics-cpp-ros2-ot-scada-bess`)

> **Group:** IV. Physical-Cyber: Automotive, EV Charging, Robotics & OT
> **Product Archetypes:** Robotics_Cpp_ROS2_OT_SCADA_BESS
> **Trigger Signals:** ros2, rclcpp, rclpy, dds, zmq, zeromq, modbus, opcua, plc, scada, robot, actuator, motor, cpp, cmake

## [ BLOCK: cpp-memory-safety-and-zmq-deserialization ]
### C/C++ Memory Safety (`memcpy`, Buffer Overflow, Integer Overflow) & ZeroMQ/Protobuf Parsing
- Inspect C/C++ network/IPC handlers (ZeroMQ `zmq_recv`, raw UDP/TCP sockets, serial/CAN frames, custom binary headers, Protobuf/FlatBuffers) for unchecked lengths passed to `memcpy`, `strcpy`, `sprintf`, fixed-size stack buffers, `new uint8_t[len]` integer overflows, and use-after-free across async callbacks.

## [ BLOCK: ros2-dds-zmq-unauthenticated-actuation ]
### ROS2 DDS / ZeroMQ Unauthenticated Pub/Sub & Physical Actuator Command Injection
- Check whether ROS2 nodes (`rclcpp`, `rclpy`) enforce SROS2 DDS security enclaves (`governance.xml`, `permissions.xml`) or whether ZeroMQ sockets (`ZMQ_SUB`, `ZMQ_PULL`, `ZMQ_REP`) bind to `tcp://0.0.0.0:*` without CurveZMQ encryption/authentication.
- Trace whether an attacker on the local network or via a cloud-to-robot WebRTC/WebSocket bridge can publish directly to `/cmd_vel`, `/joint_trajectory`, `/gripper_cmd`, or low-level motor torque topics.

## [ BLOCK: ot-modbus-opcua-plc-and-emergency-stop-interlock ]
### OT/SCADA (Modbus TCP, OPC-UA, S7comm), Watchdog Starvation & E-Stop Bypass
- Inspect bridges between IT/Cloud APIs and OT fieldbus protocols (Modbus TCP `:502`, OPC-UA `:4840`, EtherCAT, CANopen, PROFINET) in factories, BESS grid controllers, or automated lines.
- Verify 3 physical safety invariants in code:
  1. **Kinematic / Torque / Thermal Clamping:** Are joint angles, velocities, torques, voltages, and currents clamped to safe envelopes before hardware write?
  2. **Dead-Man Switch / Heartbeat Watchdog:** If the high-level planner (`vla.cpp` / cloud bridge) crashes or loses connection, does the low-level controller enter a safe stop state within `N ms`?
  3. **E-Stop Independence:** Ensure software APIs cannot override or clear a hardware Emergency Stop without physical reset.

### Standard Mappings
- IEC-62443-4-2, ISO-SAE-21434, ISO-10218, ASVS-5.0-V2-Validation, ASVS-5.0-V11-Cryptography, ASVS-5.0-V13-Configuration, CWE-119, CWE-120, CWE-306, CWE-787

### Safe Patterns (Refutation Anchors)
- C++ bounds-checked buffers (std::array, std::span, std::snprintf) with explicit payload size validation before Protobuf ParseFromArray() or FlatBuffersVerifier check
- SROS2 enclaves with DDS Security (governance.xml / permissions.xml signed by CA) or ZeroMQ CurveZMQ (zmq::sockopt::curve_server) with HMAC + monotonic sequence numbers on all actuation frames
- C++/ROS2 deterministic safety supervisor clamping joint torque/velocity/acceleration and enforcing a 50ms dead-man heartbeat timer (zeroing motor torque on timeout)
- Hardware-wired E-Stop safety relay (SIL-2/SIL-3 / PL d) and unidirectional OT firewall separating IT APIs from PLC/Modbus/CAN actuation buses

### Vulnerable Patterns
- C/C++ raw memcpy(dest, zmq_msg.data(), zmq_msg.size()), strcpy, sprintf, or unchecked integer arithmetic on network/sensor frame headers causing stack/heap buffer overflow
- Unauthenticated ZeroMQ (tcp://0.0.0.0:5555) or ROS2 DDS nodes without SROS2 accepting /cmd_vel, /joint_trajectory, or motor torque commands from any host on the subnet
- Missing dead-man heartbeat watchdog in C++ motor control loop (holding last commanded velocity/torque indefinitely when ZMQ/ROS2 publisher disconnects) or software API able to override E-Stop
- Backend Python/Go/C++ service writing unvalidated setpoints directly to Modbus TCP coils/holding registers (:502) or OPC-UA nodes without bounds checking

### Mandatory Evidence (`required_evidence`)
- ev_... excerpt of C/C++/Python socket/ROS2/Modbus handler showing buffer handling, authentication, and command bounds
- ev_... excerpt of watchdog timer, kinematic clamp, or safety state machine logic

### Verification Questions When Static Code Is Inconclusive (`questions_when_unclear`)
- Is a hardware safety PLC / SIL-rated E-Stop circuit enforcing physical torque/speed/thermal cutoffs downstream of the software controller?
- Are ROS2 DDS / ZeroMQ / Modbus ports isolated on an internal robot/plant VLAN with no routing from corporate Wi-Fi or cloud tunnels?
